author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during [execution] (quote tweet of @arlanr: "Turning the entire web into a filesystem. Code hallucinations are not a model problem. They're a data problem. Every day, APIs ship breaking changes, deprecate endpoints, and rename parameters. Models can't keep up because their training...")

Share the angle that scheduling policy (not just raw capacity) is the key unlock — Nomad/HashiCorp background makes him a great person to discuss with
